title: What if gravity turned off? You're on a balcony at the equator, where...
description_full: What if gravity turned off? You're on a balcony at the equator, where the ground carries you at 1,000 mph. You wouldn't shoot into space: you'd keep flying straight while the curved Earth falls away beneath you. Cars slide with no way to brake, a dog floats past on its leash, a mother hangs on to a traffic light and her stroller, strangers cling to each other, the ocean lifts off its bed... and then gravity comes back. What would you grab first? #whatif #pov #simulation #science #physics
audio: No voiceover (faster-whisper small returned zero segments). Music/SFX bed at a steady ~-22 dB RMS 0-44s; rumble swells to ~-11 dB at 46-50s (planet swells / ground cracks); drops to ~-29 dB at 52-56s ('For a moment, nothing falls'); surges to ~-10 dB at 58-63s (gravity returns, impact); decays to near-silence by 72s; true silence on the black frame 72.6-73.6s; quiet tone under the end card. TikTok track listed as 'son original' by 'What if?'.
transcript_source: burned-in captions read visually from 1 fps frames (no speech); see research/library/transcripts/7693276132128328992.txt
title_pattern: 'What if <physical constant> turned off?' question + second-person POV setup with a concrete place and a surprising number ('You're on a balcony at the equator, where the ground carries you at 1,000 mph'), then the description spoils the beat list in one run-on sentence and ends with an engagement question ('What would you grab first?'). Hashtags #whatif #pov #simulation #science #physics. Pattern: [What if X stopped?] + [You are at <specific place>] + [counter-intuitive physics fact] + [CTA question].

thumbnail.composition: TikTok cover = first frame. 9:16 high-angle POV from a balcony looking down onto a low-poly sunny beach-city intersection: orange office block top centre, sea and a lighthouse top left, zebra crossings and a traffic light in the lower half, the balcony rail corner bottom right. Title sits dead centre over the building facade; a small data HUD sits on the left edge at mid height.
thumbnail.text: 'What if gravity turned off?' in a light, elegant serif (book-style, white, ~5% frame height, 2 lines, centred). HUD: tiny tracked caps 'GRAVITY', large serif '0.997 g', tiny caps 'AT THE EQUATOR'.
thumbnail.colours: Bright daylight palette: terracotta/orange building, teal sea, pale blue sky, grey asphalt with white crosswalk stripes, small saturated accents (red car, red awning, balloon bunch, umbrellas). White text with soft shadow only.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Tiny pedestrians and toy-like cars far below vs the viewer's elevated balcony; the scale contrast is height/vertigo rather than a big subject. Calm, ordinary scene that the title promises to destroy.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Reads as a 'calm before the disaster' still: an everyday city under a question that implies everything in it is about to fly. The scientific HUD ('0.997 g') signals simulation/precision and makes it feel like a physics experiment, not a cartoon. Weak as a click-thumbnail (small text, no focal object); it relies on in-feed autoplay where the HUD number ticking down is the real hook.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: [on-screen, no VO] 'What if gravity turned off?' (0-3.5s) -> 'You are on a balcony at the equator.' (4-7s). HUD: 'GRAVITY 0.997 g / AT THE EQUATOR'.
hook.device: Question title + second-person POV placement ('You are on a balcony...') + a live scientific readout that the viewer instinctively waits to see change. The traffic light flips red->green at 3s and cars start moving: life is normal, the countdown is implied. Gravity actually hits 0 g at 10s, so the payoff of the premise lands within the first eighth of the video, and the HUD then switches to an ever-rising 'YOUR HEIGHT' number that keeps the viewer watching to see where it ends.

beats.summary: Title card over calm low-poly city from a balcony POV; HUD shows real gravity at the equator (0.997 g).
Places the viewer ('You are on a balcony at the equator') and drops the counter-intuitive fact that the ground carries you at 1,000 mph; HUD gravity starts dropping (0.902 g, SWITCHED OFF).
'Gravity just switched off.' HUD hits 0.000 g; camera begins to lift; HUD swaps to YOUR HEIGHT 37 ft ABOVE THE STREET.
Cars, people and loose objects float up past the camera ('Anything not held down floats away', 'Without weight, your grip is everything').
Close detail of people chained to a traffic light pole, holding each other ('People cling to each other', 'Let go, and nothing will stop you').

Camera tilts to the horizon: 'You fly straight. The ground curves away.' explains why you rise (tangent motion), then 'Even the ocean lifts off' with the sea rising as a slab; HUD sublabel becomes AND RISING.
Overhead over a plaza: 'You are now ten stories up.' then 'The planet itself starts to swell' as the ground cracks open; audio rumble peaks.
'For a moment, nothing falls.' Camera looks up at a tower with debris frozen mid-air; HUD sublabel FOR NOW; audio drops out.
'Then gravity comes back.' HUD becomes IMPACT IN 2.73 s / 165 FEET TO THE GROUND, ticking down; camera dives at the plaza; audio surges.
Hard impact: camera lies on the ground, cracked-screen glass overlay, dust cloud, a car lands; HUD 'THE GROUND / HERE'; image darkens.
End card repeats the title question plus a fact-check footnote (ISS gravity ~90%; astronauts are falling around Earth) that invites 'well actually' comments and rewatch.

pacing.words_per_min: No VO. On-screen caption track ~85 words (incl. title twice, excl. footnote) over 80 s = ~64 words/min read-speed; ~105 incl. footnote.
pacing.caption_cadence: 13 caption lines, each 4-7 words, held 3-5 s; gaps of ~1 s between lines; a new line (or new HUD sublabel) roughly every 4 s.
pacing.avg_shot_length_s: Essentially one continuous simulated camera (scene-cut detector finds only the impact at 62.2 s). Counting visual setups (reframes/tilts), ~21 setups in 80 s = ~3.8 s each; the HUD number changes every frame so there is never a static moment.
pacing.structure_timing_pct: premise payoff at 12% (10 s), physics reveal at 38%, planetary escalation at 49-64%, false calm at 65%, reversal at 74%, impact at 78%, end card at 92%.

techniques_worth_copying: Live data HUD as the retention engine: one big serif number with a tiny caps label and sublabel (GRAVITY 0.997 g -> YOUR HEIGHT 37 ft -> IMPACT IN 2.73 s -> THE GROUND HERE). The metric changes meaning at each act; the sublabel alone tells the story (AT THE EQUATOR, SWITCHED OFF, ABOVE THE STREET, AND RISING, FOR NOW).
Second-person POV with a single continuous camera: the viewer IS the character; height increases monotonically so the viewer always wants to see the next number.
Short, calm, literary captions (italic serif, 4-7 words) instead of hype text; understated tone contrasts with the chaos and feels premium.
One counter-intuitive physics line mid-video ('You fly straight. The ground curves away.') that reframes the premise and earns 'I learned something' saves.
Escalation ladder: objects -> people -> ocean -> planet; each step bigger in scale.
False calm before reversal: audio drop + 'For a moment, nothing falls.' + HUD 'FOR NOW', then a countdown timer to impact ('IMPACT IN 2.73 s').
Impact rendered as a cracked screen overlay on the POV lens, then 1 s of black silence before the end card.
End card repeats the title question and adds a fact-check footnote that sparks comments; description ends with 'What would you grab first?' CTA.
code_only_remake_needs: Scene: a stylised 2.5D/isometric city block done in SVG/Canvas (flat-shaded low-poly look via polygon facades, crosswalk stripes, palms, sea band, sky gradient). True 3D like the original is out of scope; fake it with layered parallax planes (street plane, building facades, sky) and a camera that scales/translates layers to simulate rising, tilting toward the horizon, and diving.

Floating-objects system: sprites for cars (boxy SVG), people (stick/ragdoll figures with 4 limbs rotating), umbrellas, dumpsters, a dog on a leash; per-object upward velocity, spin and drift with seeded randomness; 'attached' objects (traffic-light chain of people) use simple spring/pendulum constraints.
HUD component: tiny tracked caps label + big serif number + caps sublabel, driven by an interpolated value per frame (gravity g, height ft, impact countdown s) with label swaps at act boundaries.
Caption component: centred italic serif lines with soft shadow, fade in/out over ~0.3 s, positioned lower-middle; title card variant in non-italic serif.

Effects: ground-crack SVG paths drawn on with stroke-dashoffset and widened over time; ocean-sheet lift (displaced wave polygon rising); camera shake; dive with motion-blur streaks; impact flash + cracked-glass overlay (radial line bursts) + dust (blurred noise blobs) + vignette fade to black.

Audio: ambient bed, low rumble swell, silence drop, whoosh/impact hit, then silence. Can use synthesized or royalty-free SFX; optional Kokoro VO reading the captions (the original has none, so captions-only is a valid format).
Timeline data: ~13 caption beats with HUD keyframes; one storyboard JSON drives captions, HUD values, camera keyframes and object spawn waves.
notes: Control sample (outlier 0.86, slightly under channel median). Labelled 'AI-generated' by TikTok; visuals look like a real-time 3D game-engine simulation (low-poly city, ragdoll physics), not generative video. No speech. Study structure only; do not reuse visuals/text.
